name: London
tagline: London's oldest restaurant, since 1798, and the fish and chips that hasn't changed since 1914.

Rules.description: London's oldest restaurant, since 1798. Dickens and Charlie Chaplin both dined within its walls.

The Golden Hind.description: Traditional fish and chips in Marylebone since 1914.

Core by Clare Smyth.description: Clare Smyth, the first and only British female chef with three Michelin stars, in Notting Hill.

Borough Market.description: One of London's oldest food markets, with more than a thousand years of history next to London Bridge.

St. John.description: The restaurant that popularized nose-to-tail cooking, in Smithfield. Anthony Bourdain called it his dream restaurant. One Michelin star.

Restaurant Gordon Ramsay.description: Gordon Ramsay's flagship restaurant in Chelsea, holding three Michelin stars since 2001, serving precise contemporary French cuisine.

Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester.description: French haute cuisine by chef Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester hotel in Mayfair, holding two Michelin stars.

Sketch (Lecture Room & Library).description: Sketch's iconic Gallery, with its egg-shaped bathroom pods and India Mahdavi's pink interior, went viral on social media; its Lecture Room & Library holds two Michelin stars.

Hélène Darroze at The Connaught.description: French chef Hélène Darroze leads the kitchen at The Connaught hotel in Mayfair, holding two Michelin stars.

The Ledbury.description: Top-tier modern British cooking in Notting Hill, holding two Michelin stars and widely considered one of London's best restaurants.

Ikoyi.description: West African-inspired tasting menus by chef Jeremy Chan, holding two Michelin stars, in St James's.

Kitchen Table.description: An intimate counter with just a handful of seats beside the kitchen in Fitzrovia, holding two Michelin stars.

The Clove Club.description: One of the restaurants that redefined casual fine dining in Shoreditch, holding one Michelin star, inside the historic town hall.

Brat.description: Basque-influenced wood-fired grill in Shoreditch, famous for its whole roasted turbot; one Michelin star.

Lyle's.description: Seasonal British cooking on a daily fixed menu in Shoreditch, from chef James Lowe; one Michelin star.

Trinity.description: Neighbourhood restaurant in Clapham from chef Adam Byatt, serving modern British food with one Michelin star.

Sushi Tetsu.description: A tiny seven-seat sushi counter in Clerkenwell, one of the hardest reservations to get in London; one Michelin star.

Marcus.description: Marcus Wareing's flagship restaurant at The Berkeley hotel, serving refined British food with one Michelin star.

Pied à Terre.description: One of London's longest-running fine-dining restaurants, open on Charlotte Street since 1991, holding one Michelin star.

A. Wong.description: Modern regional Chinese cooking in Pimlico from chef Andrew Wong, with a celebrated dim sum brunch; one Michelin star.

Kai Mayfair.description: Upscale Chinese cuisine in Mayfair, holding one Michelin star since 2011.

Umu.description: High-end Japanese kaiseki cuisine in Mayfair, holding two Michelin stars.

City Social.description: Jason Atherton's restaurant on the 24th floor of Tower 42, with panoramic views over the City and one Michelin star.

Galvin La Chapelle.description: Classic French cooking from the Galvin brothers inside a former Victorian chapel in Spitalfields; one Michelin star.

Dinner by Heston Blumenthal.description: Heston Blumenthal reinterprets historic British recipes at the Mandarin Oriental in Knightsbridge; two Michelin stars.

Portland.description: Seasonal, ingredient-led British cooking in Fitzrovia, holding one Michelin star.

Angler.description: Seafood restaurant atop the South Place Hotel in the City, holding one Michelin star.

Trishna.description: Contemporary Indian cooking focused on west-coast seafood, in Marylebone; one Michelin star.

Gymkhana.description: Indian cuisine inspired by colonial-era hunting clubs, in Mayfair, holding one Michelin star.

Jamavar.description: Indian cuisine drawing on regions across the subcontinent, in Mayfair, holding one Michelin star.

Benares.description: Modern Indian cuisine from chef Atul Kochhar on Berkeley Square, holding one Michelin star.

Kiln.description: Charcoal-grilled Thai cooking served along a narrow counter in Soho, recognised with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

The Five Fields.description: An intimate Chelsea restaurant with a seasonal tasting menu; one Michelin star.

Endo at The Rotunda.description: Precision sushi omakase from chef Endo Kazutoshi in White City, holding two Michelin stars.

Le Gavroche.description: Founded in 1967 by the Roux brothers, one of London's most influential classic French restaurants; two Michelin stars.

Pollen Street Social.description: Jason Atherton's Mayfair restaurant that helped define upscale casual dining; one Michelin star.

The River Cafe.description: Riverside Italian cooking in Hammersmith, founded by Ruth Rogers and the late Rose Gray, a training ground for many British chefs.

Chez Bruce.description: A Wandsworth neighbourhood restaurant repeatedly voted a Londoner favourite for its Anglo-French cooking.

La Trompette.description: A Chiswick neighbourhood restaurant with Franco-European cooking well regarded by local critics.

The Glasshouse.description: Modern British restaurant in Kew, holding one Michelin star.

Scott's.description: Upscale seafood restaurant in Mayfair, with history dating back to 1851 and regulars ranging back to Ian Fleming.

J Sheekey.description: Classic seafood restaurant in Covent Garden's Theatreland, open since the late 19th century.

Bentley's Oyster Bar & Grill.description: Oyster bar and seafood restaurant in Mayfair since 1916, long helmed by chef Richard Corrigan.

Wiltons.description: One of London's oldest seafood restaurants, with roots dating back to 1742, in St James's.

Simpson's in the Strand.description: A London institution since 1828, famous for roast meats carved tableside from silver trolleys.

The Ivy.description: Iconic Covent Garden restaurant frequented by the theatre and film world since 1917.

Quo Vadis.description: Historic Soho restaurant in a building where Karl Marx once lived, serving modern British food.

Andrew Edmunds.description: A small, candlelit Soho restaurant, a quiet favourite of local food critics since the 1980s.

Bob Bob Ricard.description: A Soho restaurant famous for the "Press for Champagne" button at every table and its Art Deco-style interiors.

The Wolseley.description: A grand European-style café-brasserie on Piccadilly, set inside a 1920s former car showroom.

Dishoom Covent Garden.description: A chain inspired by Bombay's old Irani cafés, famous for its queues and its bacon naan roll.

Barrafina Soho.description: A no-reservations Spanish tapas counter on Dean Street, one of London's most acclaimed Spanish restaurants.

Padella.description: Handmade fresh pasta at accessible prices next to Borough Market, famous for its long queues.

Flat Iron.description: A chain that popularised the affordable, fixed-price flat iron steak in London.

Hawksmoor Seven Dials.description: A British steakhouse serving dry-aged native-breed beef, one of London's most celebrated steak chains.

Smokestak.description: American-style wood-smoked barbecue in Shoreditch, celebrated for its ribs and brisket.

Temper Soho.description: A basement whole-animal barbecue restaurant in Soho, cooking meat over live fire.

Bao Soho.description: The Taiwanese restaurant that popularised the filled bao bun in London, with regular queues on Lexington Street.

Kricket Soho.description: Modern Indian small plates, born as a food truck and now one of Soho's favourites.

Berber & Q.description: North African and Middle Eastern-inspired barbecue under railway arches in Haggerston.

Morito.description: Spanish and eastern Mediterranean tapas bar on Exmouth Market, the smaller sibling of Moro.

Moro.description: Cuisine fusing Spain and North Africa on Exmouth Market, a critics' favourite since 1997.

Ottolenghi Islington.description: Yotam Ottolenghi's first shop, in Islington, with its famous salad counter and Mediterranean pastries.

Rochelle Canteen.description: A restaurant tucked inside a former Shoreditch schoolyard, serving simple seasonal British food.

Towpath Cafe.description: A small café beside Regent's Canal in Hackney, open only in the warmer months, much loved by local critics.

Tayyabs.description: A Whitechapel Pakistani institution since 1972, famous for its grilled lamb chops; there is always a queue.

Needoo Grill.description: A Whitechapel Pakistani grill, often compared to neighbouring Tayyabs for its skewers and curries.

Lahore Kebab House.description: One of Whitechapel's oldest Pakistani restaurants, open since 1972.

Aladin Brick Lane.description: One of the classic curry houses of Brick Lane, London's most famous Indian and Bangladeshi street.

Beigel Bake.description: A 24-hour Jewish bakery on Brick Lane open since the 1970s, famous for its salt beef bagel; Anthony Bourdain visited it on No Reservations.

Four Seasons Chinatown.description: Cantonese roast duck restaurant on Gerrard Street, one of Chinatown's most celebrated.

Yauatcha.description: A dim sum and tea house in Soho, holding one Michelin star, from the Hakkasan group.

Hakkasan Hanway Place.description: An upscale Chinese basement restaurant in Fitzrovia that helped redefine fine Chinese dining in London; one Michelin star.

Din Tai Fung Covent Garden.description: The world-famous Taiwanese chain known for its soup dumplings, with its first London site in Covent Garden.

The Palomar.description: Modern Israeli cooking at a lively Soho counter, inspired by Jerusalem.

Nopi.description: Yotam Ottolenghi's Soho restaurant serving Mediterranean and Middle Eastern sharing plates.

Song Que.description: A classic Vietnamese restaurant on Kingsland Road, in the heart of Shoreditch's "Pho Mile".

Mangal Ocakbasi.description: A Turkish ocakbasi grill in Dalston, a benchmark of neighbourhood Turkish cooking in London since the 1990s.

Franco Manca Brixton.description: The original Franco Manca pizzeria, born in Brixton Market with slow-fermented sourdough.

Pizza Pilgrims Dean Street.description: A Neapolitan pizzeria that began life as a family food truck, with its first permanent site in Soho.

Neal's Yard Dairy.description: A reference point for artisan British and Irish cheese next to Borough Market, since 1979.

Monmouth Coffee.description: A pioneering specialty coffee roaster and café at Borough Market.

Wright Brothers Borough Market.description: An oyster and seafood bar next to Borough Market, serving oysters from its own Cornwall beds.

Roast Borough Market.description: A British restaurant overlooking Borough Market, sourcing meat and vegetables from market traders below.

Poppies Fish & Chips.description: 1940s-style fish and chips in Spitalfields, with vintage decor and a traditional chippy atmosphere.

Golden Union Fish Bar.description: Classic fish and chips in Soho, repeatedly voted among London's best.

Masters Super Fish.description: A neighbourhood chippy near Waterloo, much loved by local critics for its generous portions.

Duck & Waffle.description: A restaurant open 24 hours on the 40th floor of Heron Tower, with panoramic views over London.

Aqua Shard.description: A restaurant on the 31st floor of The Shard, serving British food with views over the Thames.

Fortnum & Mason Diamond Jubilee Tea Salo.description: The tea salon of Fortnum & Mason department store on Piccadilly, a London afternoon tea institution since 1707.

The Ritz Restaurant.description: The Ritz hotel's gilded ballroom-like dining room on Piccadilly, serving classic French cuisine with one Michelin star.

Claridge's Restaurant.description: The main restaurant of Claridge's hotel in Mayfair, an emblem of London hotel luxury since the 19th century.

Brown's Hotel English Tea Room.description: The classic tea room of Brown's Hotel in Mayfair, one of London's oldest hotels.

The Savoy Grill.description: The Savoy hotel's historic dining room, run by Gordon Ramsay, serving classic British and French food.

American Bar at The Savoy.description: Considered one of the world's oldest and most elegant cocktail bars, inside the Savoy hotel since the late 19th century.

Connaught Bar.description: The cocktail bar of The Connaught hotel in Mayfair, a regular fixture on lists of the world's best bars.

Dukes Bar.description: The martini bar of Dukes Hotel in St James's, famous for mixing the cocktail tableside for guests.

Nightjar.description: A speakeasy-style basement cocktail bar in Shoreditch, with live music and craft cocktails.

Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese.description: A historic Fleet Street pub rebuilt in 1667 after the Great Fire of London, once frequented by Samuel Johnson and Charles Dickens.

The Blackfriar.description: An Art Nouveau-style pub next to Blackfriars station, with a uniquely sculpted facade and interior in London.
